items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: Tony Bennett wanted me to replace Ralph — what was the guy? ... Sharon. Ralph Sharon? ... I didn’t take the gig because I wanted to do my own thing man. I told him I would fill in for him until he could get somebody.

ctx.x: This is great. A little while ago you used the word “comping.” I wanted to ask you about comping behind Joe Williams and Nancy Wilson and Jimmy Witherspoon. How does a piano player learn to be an accompanist that vocalists want to work with?

Well without getting real technical, the main way would be listen. Listening. And you have to have your voice leading together so that you’re playing contrapuntally. So the basis of simple counterpoint is when the main theme is moving, you’re standing still. When that stops then you move. And so I would listen to something the vocalist did and then play in between the phrases, and then we’d lock up together. And so the singers all like to work with me.
